The core innovation lies in combining online learning with horizon smoothing to handle structural breaks in post-COVID electricity demand. The smoothed BOA algorithm dynamically adjusts weights based on instantaneous loss gradients while maintaining stability through P-spline smoothing across forecast horizons. This ensures that even if individual experts perform poorly in certain periods (e.g., during lockdowns), their influence is dampened over time rather than discarded entirely. The holiday adjustment frontend removes known shocks from the data stream, allowing downstream models to focus on underlying patterns. These primitives together form a robust framework for adaptive forecasting where both model flexibility and data integrity are preserved. Failure modes include over-smoothing leading to sluggish adaptation, or poor holiday detection causing residual anomalies. The method’s strength lies in its ability to maintain performance under changing regimes without requiring explicit regime-switching mechanisms.
